subject.probability-theory.title: Probability theory
subject.probability-theory.define: Measure-theoretic probability, limit laws, conditional expectation, martingales and stochastic processes.
subject.probability-theory.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.probability-theory.assumed_background: Measure and integration, Lp spaces, elementary real analysis and linear algebra.
subject.probability-theory.learning_outcomes:
- Identify the convergence mode and moment assumptions in each limit law.
- Formulate conditioning as an almost-everywhere integral identity.
- Check filtration, stopping-time and integrability conditions before stochastic calculations.
subject.probability-theory.study_route: [Probability spaces and random variables](./notes/pr.space.md) → [Independence and product laws](./notes/pr.independence.md) → [Modes of convergence](./notes/pr.convergence.md) → [Strong law of large numbers](./notes/pr.slln.md) → [Central limit theorem](./notes/pr.clt.md) → [Conditional expectation](./notes/pr.conditional.md) → [Filtrations and martingales](./notes/pr.martingale.md) → [Optional stopping](./notes/pr.stopping.md) → [Brownian motion](./notes/pr.brownian.md)

subject.probability-theory.references:

- **PR2** — University of Cambridge, DPMMS. [Probability and Measure](https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/study/II/Probability%2BMeasure/2019-2020/lecture-notes-1-18.pdf). 2019–2020, lectures 1–18.

pr.space.title: Probability spaces and random variables
pr.space.define: Random variables are measurable maps whose laws are probability measures.
pr.space.statement: A probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ is a measure space of mass one. A random variable is a measurable map to a measurable state space; its law is the pushforward measure.
pr.space.hypotheses: Events must belong to the chosen sigma-algebra.
pr.space.example: Real random variables have laws on the Borel sets of the real line.
pr.space.caution: A random variable and its law are different objects.
pr.space.references:
PR: probability spaces.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.independence.title: Independence and product laws
pr.independence.define: Sigma-algebras are independent when probabilities of intersections factor for every finite subfamily. Variables are independent when their generated sigma-algebras are independent.
pr.independence.statement: Sigma-algebras are independent when probabilities of intersections factor for every finite subfamily. Variables are independent when their generated sigma-algebras are independent.
pr.independence.hypotheses: Mutual independence requires more than pairwise independence.
pr.independence.example: Two independent fair bits and their sum modulo two are pairwise independent but not mutually independent.
pr.independence.caution: Zero covariance alone does not imply independence.
pr.independence.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Probability spaces and random variables](./notes/pr.space.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Tonelli and Fubini](./notes/ra.fubini.md) — Real analysis
pr.independence.references:
PR: independence.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.convergence.title: Modes of convergence
pr.convergence.define: Almost-sure, probability, distribution and mean convergence are distinct notions.
pr.convergence.statement: Almost-sure convergence implies convergence in probability, which implies convergence in distribution. $L^p$ convergence for $p\ge1$ implies convergence in probability.
pr.convergence.hypotheses: Almost-sure and probability convergence compare variables on one probability space; convergence in law compares distributions.
pr.convergence.example: Rare tall spikes may converge in probability without converging in mean.
pr.convergence.caution: Convergence in law generally does not imply convergence in probability.
pr.convergence.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Probability spaces and random variables](./notes/pr.space.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Lp spaces](./notes/ra.lp.md) — Real analysis
pr.convergence.references:
PR: convergence modes.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.borel-cantelli.title: Borel–Cantelli lemmas
pr.borel-cantelli.define: Summable event probabilities prevent infinitely many occurrences almost surely.
pr.borel-cantelli.statement: If $\sum_n\mathbb P(A_n)<\infty$, only finitely many $A_n$ occur almost surely. If the events are independent and the sum diverges, infinitely many occur almost surely.
pr.borel-cantelli.hypotheses: Independence is needed for the second conclusion in this version.
pr.borel-cantelli.example: Independent fair tosses produce infinitely many heads almost surely.
pr.borel-cantelli.caution: Divergence of the sum for dependent events does not suffice.
pr.borel-cantelli.proof_idea: A union bound proves the first part; independence and a product bound prove the second.
pr.borel-cantelli.references:
PR: Borel-Cantelli lemmas.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.slln.title: Strong law of large numbers
pr.slln.define: Independent identically distributed integrable averages converge almost surely to the mean.
pr.slln.statement: For iid real variables with $\mathbb E|X_1|<\infty$, $n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^nX_k\to\mathbb E X_1$ almost surely.
pr.slln.hypotheses: The variables are independent, identically distributed and absolutely integrable.
pr.slln.example: Empirical event frequencies converge to their probabilities.
pr.slln.caution: Finite variance is unnecessary, but an undefined mean cannot appear as the limit here.
pr.slln.proof_idea: Truncate large values, control centered partial sums, apply Borel–Cantelli and remove truncation.
pr.slln.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Borel–Cantelli lemmas](./notes/pr.borel-cantelli.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Lebesgue integration](./notes/ra.integral.md) — Real analysis
pr.slln.references:
PR: laws of large numbers.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.characteristic.title: Characteristic functions
pr.characteristic.define: Fourier transforms of probability laws encode distributions and independent sums.
pr.characteristic.statement: The function $\varphi_X(t)=\mathbb E e^{itX}$ determines the law of a real variable. Independence turns characteristic functions of sums into products.
pr.characteristic.hypotheses: The bounded exponential ensures existence for every real random variable.
pr.characteristic.caution: Moment-generating functions, unlike characteristic functions, need not exist near zero.
pr.characteristic.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Independence and product laws](./notes/pr.independence.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Plancherel theorem](./notes/ra.fourier.md) — Real analysis
pr.characteristic.references:
PR: characteristic functions.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.weak.title: Weak convergence and Portmanteau
pr.weak.define: Weak convergence is tested by bounded continuous functions and closed-set inequalities.
pr.weak.statement: For Borel probability measures on a metric space, weak convergence means convergence of integrals of all bounded continuous real functions. Equivalently, $\limsup_n\mu_n(F)\le\mu(F)$ for every closed F.
pr.weak.hypotheses: The measures live on the same metric space.
pr.weak.example: Probabilities converge for sets whose boundary has limiting measure zero.
pr.weak.caution: Integrals of unbounded continuous functions need not converge.
pr.weak.proof_idea: Approximate closed-set indicators by distance cutoffs and use level-set bounds for the converse.
pr.weak.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Modes of convergence](./notes/pr.convergence.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Topological spaces and continuity](./notes/tp.spaces.md) — Topology
pr.weak.references:
PR: weak convergence.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.clt.title: Central limit theorem
pr.clt.define: Finite-variance independent identically distributed sums have a Gaussian scaling limit.
pr.clt.statement: For iid real variables with mean $\mu$ and variance $0<\sigma^2<\infty$, $(\sum_{k=1}^nX_k-n\mu)/(\sigma\sqrt n)$ converges in law to $N(0,1)$.
pr.clt.hypotheses: This version assumes finite, strictly positive variance.
pr.clt.example: Standardized binomial counts approach the normal law.
pr.clt.caution: Infinite-variance laws may require different scaling and different limits.
pr.clt.proof_idea: Expand the characteristic function at zero to second order and apply its continuity theorem.
pr.clt.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Characteristic functions](./notes/pr.characteristic.md)
- [Weak convergence and Portmanteau](./notes/pr.weak.md)
pr.clt.references:
PR: central limit theorem.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.conditional.title: Conditional expectation
pr.conditional.define: Conditional expectation matches integrals on all events observable in a sub-sigma-algebra.
pr.conditional.statement: For $X\in L^1$ and a sub-sigma-algebra $\mathcal G$, there is a $\mathcal G$-measurable integrable Y such that $\int_A Y\,d\mathbb P=\int_A X\,d\mathbb P$ for all $A\in\mathcal G$. It is unique almost surely and denoted $\mathbb E[X\mid\mathcal G]$.
pr.conditional.hypotheses: Equality and uniqueness are modulo null sets.
pr.conditional.example: For a finite partition, conditioning averages over cells of positive probability.
pr.conditional.caution: The elementary ratio formula cannot condition directly on a probability-zero event.
pr.conditional.proof_idea: Apply Radon–Nikodym to positive and negative parts on the sub-sigma-algebra.
pr.conditional.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Probability spaces and random variables](./notes/pr.space.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Radon–Nikodym theorem](./notes/ra.rn.md) — Real analysis
pr.conditional.references:
PR: conditional expectation.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.regular.title: Regular conditional distributions
pr.regular.define: For random elements X,Y in standard Borel spaces, the conditional law of X given Y admits a probability-kernel version K(y,A) satisfying the conditional integral identities.
pr.regular.statement: For random elements X,Y in standard Borel spaces, the conditional law of X given Y admits a probability-kernel version K(y,A) satisfying the conditional integral identities.
pr.regular.hypotheses: A standard Borel space is measurably isomorphic to a Borel subset of a Polish space.
pr.regular.example: Conditional densities, when available, give concrete kernels.
pr.regular.caution: Versions can differ on Y-null sets; arbitrary measurable spaces need not admit such kernels.
pr.regular.proof_idea: Construct conditional probabilities on a countable determining family and extend to measures.
pr.regular.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Conditional expectation](./notes/pr.conditional.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Metric and Polish spaces](./notes/tp.metric.md) — Topology
pr.regular.references:
PR: regular conditional probabilities.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.ui.title: Uniform integrability
pr.ui.define: Uniform tail control is the missing ingredient for convergence in mean.
pr.ui.statement: A family $\mathcal X\subset L^1$ is uniformly integrable if $\sup_{X\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E[|X|1_{|X|>K}]\to0$. For integrable X, convergence in probability plus uniform integrability of the sequence is equivalent to $L^1$ convergence.
pr.ui.hypotheses: All variables are on one probability space.
pr.ui.example: A uniform Lp bound for some p greater than one implies uniform integrability.
pr.ui.caution: Uniform L1 boundedness alone allows rare tall spikes and is insufficient.
pr.ui.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Modes of convergence](./notes/pr.convergence.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Lp spaces](./notes/ra.lp.md) — Real analysis
pr.ui.references:
PR: uniform integrability.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.martingale.title: Filtrations and martingales
pr.martingale.define: A martingale preserves its conditional mean as information grows.
pr.martingale.statement: A filtration is an increasing sequence $\mathcal F_n$ of sigma-algebras. An integrable adapted process is a martingale if $\mathbb E[M_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=M_n$ almost surely.
pr.martingale.hypotheses: The filtration is part of the data.
pr.martingale.example: Centered partial sums of independent integrable increments form a martingale.
pr.martingale.caution: Martingales need not have independent increments.
pr.martingale.references:
PR: martingales.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.doob.title: Doob maximal inequality
pr.doob.define: A terminal Lp bound controls the maximum along a finite martingale path.
pr.doob.statement: For a discrete-time martingale, finite horizon n and $p>1$, $\|\max_{0\le k\le n}|M_k|\|_p\le p/(p-1)\,\|M_n\|_p$.
pr.doob.hypotheses: The terminal value is in Lp.
pr.doob.example: The terminal Lp size controls the maximum along a finite path.
pr.doob.caution: The strong inequality has no finite constant of this form at p = 1.
pr.doob.proof_idea: Stop at the first threshold crossing, bound the tail and integrate using Holder's inequality.
pr.doob.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Filtrations and martingales](./notes/pr.martingale.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Hölder and Minkowski inequalities](./notes/ra.holder.md) — Real analysis
pr.doob.references:
PR: maximal inequalities.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.stopping.title: Optional stopping
pr.stopping.define: Optional stopping preserves martingale identities under boundedness or uniform integrability.
pr.stopping.statement: For a discrete-time martingale and bounded stopping times $S\le T$, $\mathbb E[M_T\mid\mathcal F_S]=M_S$. The same holds for almost-surely finite S,T when the martingale is uniformly integrable.
pr.stopping.hypotheses: Stopping times cannot depend on future information; integrability controls passage to limits.
pr.stopping.example: Stopping an integrable fair game before a fixed round preserves expected capital.
pr.stopping.caution: An unbounded doubling strategy lacks the required integrability control.
pr.stopping.proof_idea: Sum stopped increments at finite horizons, then use uniform integrability for unbounded horizons.
pr.stopping.references:
PR: optional stopping.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.martingale-limit.title: Martingale convergence
pr.martingale-limit.define: L1-bounded martingales converge almost surely; uniform integrability strengthens the limit.
pr.martingale-limit.statement: If $\sup_n\mathbb E|M_n|<\infty$, a discrete-time martingale converges almost surely to an integrable limit. Under uniform integrability it also converges in $L^1$ and $M_n=\mathbb E[M_\infty\mid\mathcal F_n]$.
pr.martingale-limit.hypotheses: L1 boundedness and uniform integrability have distinct consequences.
pr.martingale-limit.example: Nonnegative martingales converge almost surely but can lose expectation in the limit.
pr.martingale-limit.caution: L1 boundedness alone does not ensure L1 convergence.
pr.martingale-limit.proof_idea: The upcrossing inequality excludes oscillation; Fatou gives integrability and uniform integrability justifies the conditional limit.
pr.martingale-limit.references:
PR: martingale convergence.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.markov.title: Finite-state Markov chains
pr.markov.define: An irreducible finite-state Markov chain has a unique stationary probability vector. If also aperiodic, its distribution converges to that vector from every initial distribution.
pr.markov.statement: An irreducible finite-state Markov chain has a unique stationary probability vector. If also aperiodic, its distribution converges to that vector from every initial distribution.
pr.markov.hypotheses: Transition-matrix rows sum to one; irreducibility means all states communicate.
pr.markov.example: Deterministic alternation between two states is irreducible but periodic.
pr.markov.caution: Stationarity alone does not guarantee convergence.
pr.markov.proof_idea: Irreducibility yields the stationary eigenvector; aperiodicity removes other peripheral eigenvalues.
pr.markov.references:
PR: Markov chains.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.extension.title: Kolmogorov extension theorem
pr.extension.define: A consistent family of finite-dimensional probability laws on products of standard Borel state spaces determines a unique probability measure on the cylinder sigma-algebra of the full product.
pr.extension.statement: A consistent family of finite-dimensional probability laws on products of standard Borel state spaces determines a unique probability measure on the cylinder sigma-algebra of the full product.
pr.extension.hypotheses: Marginalization and coordinate permutations preserve the prescribed laws.
pr.extension.example: Consistent Gaussian laws of covariance min(s,t) specify Brownian finite-dimensional distributions.
pr.extension.caution: Extension alone does not give continuous sample paths.
pr.extension.proof_idea: Define cylinder probabilities and use the state-space regularity to establish the countable additivity needed for extension.
pr.extension.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Probability spaces and random variables](./notes/pr.space.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Measure spaces](./notes/ra.measure.md) — Real analysis
pr.extension.references:
PR: construction of processes.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.brownian.title: Brownian motion
pr.brownian.define: Brownian motion has continuous paths and independent Gaussian increments.
pr.brownian.statement: Standard Brownian motion starts at zero, has continuous paths and independent stationary increments with $B_t-B_s\sim N(0,t-s)$ for $0\le s<t$.
pr.brownian.hypotheses: For stochastic calculus the filtration must make future increments independent of present information.
pr.brownian.caution: Paths are almost surely nowhere differentiable despite continuity.
pr.brownian.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Kolmogorov extension theorem](./notes/pr.extension.md)
- [Independence and product laws](./notes/pr.independence.md)
pr.brownian.references:
PR: Brownian motion.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.ito-integral.title: Itô integral and isometry
pr.ito-integral.define: The Brownian stochastic integral is constructed by an L2 isometry.
pr.ito-integral.statement: For predictable H with $\mathbb E\int_0^T H_t^2dt<\infty$, the Brownian integral obeys $\mathbb E(\int_0^T H_t\,dB_t)^2=\mathbb E\int_0^T H_t^2dt$.
pr.ito-integral.hypotheses: Use a Brownian filtration with the usual conditions and square integrability in time and probability.
pr.ito-integral.caution: This is not ordinary integration against a path of bounded variation.
pr.ito-integral.proof_idea: Define the integral on adapted step processes, prove the isometry by independent increments and complete in L2.
pr.ito-integral.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Brownian motion](./notes/pr.brownian.md)
- [Filtrations and martingales](./notes/pr.martingale.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Hilbert spaces and orthogonal projection](./notes/fa.hilbert.md) — Functional analysis
pr.ito-integral.references:
PR: stochastic integration.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.

pr.ito-formula.title: Itô's formula
pr.ito-formula.define: The stochastic chain rule includes a second-order quadratic-variation correction.
pr.ito-formula.statement: For $f\in C^{1,2}([0,T]\times\mathbb R)$, $df(t,B_t)=(f_t+\tfrac12f_{xx})(t,B_t)dt+f_x(t,B_t)dB_t$, locally when global integrability is unavailable.
pr.ito-formula.hypotheses: One continuous time derivative and two continuous spatial derivatives suffice in this version.
pr.ito-formula.caution: The second-derivative term records quadratic variation and cannot be omitted.
pr.ito-formula.proof_idea: Taylor-expand along partitions; squared increments converge to elapsed time and higher-order remainders vanish after localization.
pr.ito-formula.references:
PR: Ito formula.

- **PR** — Rick Durrett. [Probability: Theory and Examples](https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf). Fifth-edition author manuscript, 2019.
